summary.en: Violence continues across South Sudan as an army captain and a civilian were killed in cattle-raid clashes in Abyei and seven children were released from armed forces and reunited with families in Western Equatoria. Machar confirmed Regina Joseph Kaba as acting SPLM-IO chair, denied involvement in Majur’s failed evacuation, and defended the acting leader while questioning family-visit restrictions and nighttime searches. Local actors are pursuing community solutions, with Uror communities seeking local conflict resolution and clan elders meeting over boundary disputes. The UCDP recorded two battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Vold fortsetter i Sør-Sudan da en hærkaptein og en sivil ble drept i oksekamp-konflikter i Abyei, og syv barn ble løslatt fra væpnede styrker og gjenforent med familiene i Vest-Equatoria. Machar bekreftet Regina Joseph Kaba som fungerende SPLM-IO-leder, avviste involvering i Majurs mislykkede evakuering, og forsvaret den fungerende lederen mens han stilte spørsmål ved restriksjoner på familiebesøk og nattlige ransakinger. Lokale aktører arbeider med samfunnsløsninger, med Uror-samfunn som søker lokal konfliktløsning og klaneldste som møtes om grensediskusjoner. UCDP registrerte to dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: South Sudanese Civil War
background.extract: The South Sudanese Civil War was a multi-sided civil war in South Sudan fought from 2013 to 2018 between government and opposition forces. The civil war caused rampant human rights abuses, including forced displacement, ethnic massacres, and killings of journalists by various parties. Since the war's end, South Sudan has been governed by a coalition formed by leaders of the former warring factions, Salva Kiir and Riek Machar. The country continues to recover from the war while experiencing ongoing and systemic ethnic violence.
